questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = -3 - 2(x - 2)^2$$ and $$h(x) = -3 + 2(x - 2)^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 2} f(x)$$?

options.why: Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$-3$$ as $$x \to 2$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$-3$$ too.
This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.
This is the input value being approached, not the output.

options.text: It cannot be determined without a formula for $$f$$.

questions.stem: The derivative of a function $$f$$ is $$f'(x) = (x + 1)^2(x - 4)$$. On which intervals is $$f$$ increasing?

options.why: The squared factor does not change sign at $$x = -1$$, so f′ < 0 for $$x < -1$$.
On $$-1 < x < 4$$ the factor $$x - 4$$ is negative.
Correct. The squared factor is never negative, so the sign of $$f'$$ matches $$x - 4$$.
Here f′ < 0 because $$x - 4 < 0$$.

questions.explanation: $$(x + 1)^2 \geq 0$$ for all $$x$$, so $$f'(x) > 0$$ exactly when $$x > 4$$. Note $$f'$$ does not change sign at $$-1$$, so there is no extremum there.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = \sin(3x)$$?

questions.stem: What is the total area of the regions enclosed by the graphs of $$y = x^3$$ and $$y = x$$?

questions.stem: A 15-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 1 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 9 feet from the wall?

options.why: This swaps the roles of x and y.

Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 225$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 9$$, $$y = 12$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{9(1)}{12}$$.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{9 \cdot 1}{12} = -\frac{3}{4}$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem:
